text:
sara: FYI alert from the hosted-usw2 capacity dashboard — we've seen a steady p95 admission_reject_rate ~1.8% for ~45m. queue depth spikes but GPU utilization looks normal.

mike: can you paste the dashboard snapshot? which pool and pool-size are we hitting?

sara: hosted-usw2.pool-12 (mixed-size), slot headroom down to ~6% on average. dashboard: https://dashboards/redwood/capacity/usw2/pool-12 (screenshot clipped).

raj: odd — if GPU util is normal maybe it's a KV-cache missstorm or proxy retries driving slot occupancy. any proxy errors in logs?

lin: I saw increased proxy 502s early in the window, but they recovered. logs show a burst of small embedding requests from an internal customer around t-50m.

olivia: is the admission controller configured to favor canary/priority routes? we recently pushed a routing policy that pins more traffic to pool-12 for latency experiments.

deploy-bot: @sara triggered alert: hosted-usw2/pool-12 admission_reject_rate > 1% for 30m (rule: adm_reject_p95).

sara: yes — we did a canary redirect for rts/fast-latency yesterday. might be correlated.

mike: quick probe — run a metrics query for admission rejects by route and seq_len. use the query below:

```
// prometheus-ish pseudo
sum by(route)(increase(admission_rejects_total{pool="pool-12"}[30m]))
/
sum by(route)(increase(admission_requests_total{pool="pool-12"}[30m]))
```

lin: preliminary numbers: rts/fast-latency accounts for ~60% of rejects, seqlen distribution skewed to short requests (<64). continuous batching maybe starving long-running requests?

raj: short requests are cheaper but cause lots of scheduling churn. if batching window is tuned for long tails we can get fragmentation.

olivia: ops question — do we want to enable soft-eviction (evict low-priority queued work when headroom < X) or loosen admission to accept more but defer low-priority? cost vs availability tradeoff.

mike: soft-eviction helps latency for priority routes but increases tail latency for evicted jobs and complicates billing. overprovisioning to prevent rejects is expensive.

sara: cost numbers: adding 2x slots to pool-12 would increase monthly infra by ~6k USD. soft-eviction config change is cheap but risky.

raj: can we try a middle path: enable a temporary short grace window for low-priority routes (5s) and reduce batch window for the short-request workload to avoid fragmentation?

lin: patch ready for batch-window tweak. small change: `BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=8 -> 4` for pool-12 routing class. want to canary it to pool nodes only.

olivia: I'm +1 for canary. we should also add a dashboard panel showing evictions vs rejects so we can see behavior in real-time.

sara: I'll open a rollback-safe rollout: canary 5% traffic to pool-12 nodes with reduced batch wait. watch admission_reject_rate and p99 latency for priority routes.

mike: timeline?

sara: rolling the canary now. oncall-bot: tagging rota.

oncall-bot: @oncall-team assigned to sara for 60m. runbook: /runbooks/admctrl-high-rejects.

(5m later)

lin: canary applied to 5% nodes. initial metrics look promising — admission_reject_rate on canary nodes is 0.2%. non-canary still ~1.6%.

raj: good sign. if this holds for 20m we can scale canary to 25%.

mike: also schedule a follow-up to evaluate cost of moving the rts/fast-latency traffic to a dedicated pool. might be simpler than continuous tuning.

olivia: agreed. create a short ADR with cost/ops tradeoffs and perf numbers. I can draft.

sara: will keep the thread updated. if canary degrades we'll rollback the change immediately. thanks all :thumbsup:
